senses.gloss:
Jaṣa is the name of some aquatic animal or fish in the Atharvaveda and the taittirīya Saṃhitā. The commentary on the latter text explains it by makara, probably meaning ‘dolphin.’ The word also occurs in the Gopatha brāhmaṇa.
Cf. jhaṣa.
Foot notes xi. 2, 25. There are various readings: jhaṣa, jakha, jagha.
v. 5, 13, 1.
ii. 2, 5.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 96; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 624

Jāṣkamada is the name of an unknown animal in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes xi. 9, 9. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 88.

Jās-pati occurs once in the Rigveda in the sense of the ‘head of the family.’ The abstract formed from this word, jās-patya, apparently denoting ‘lordship of children,’ is also found there.
Foot notes i. 135. 8.
Rv. v. 28, 3; x. 85, 23.
